statusDetail: Coverage-complete report across six representative public paths. Authenticated account actions, paid checkout completion and destructive account actions were not exercised because they require credentials/payment; their public entry surfaces were inspected.

page.notes: Large Swedish news publication with server-rendered homepage, section, article and search templates; a cross-origin Schibsted consent iframe appears on first load.

paths.description: Homepage and primary news-discovery surface; represents the front-page feed.
Sportbladet section/listing archetype; represents editorial section pages.

Sports article/media archetype, represented in route selection and cross-template Lighthouse/article evidence.

findings.summary: The site exposes a manual theme control but does not follow the system dark preference.
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, matchMedia was true while the body remained rgb(247,247,247) with dark text and the computed color-scheme was normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Default the theme from prefers-color-scheme, declare color-scheme, and keep the manual control as an explicit user override.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion evaluate probe confirmed the preference and still found eight running animations, each with a 1,900 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query to remove non-essential animations and stop auto-advancing or looping motion.

findings.summary: Editorial route changes do not opt into View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS or authored transition rule across the MPA navigation surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } for eligible same-origin page changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: A large consent wall obscures all editorial content on every tested primary path.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360 px screenshots show the cookie settings dialog covering almost the whole viewport before any interaction; mobile controls are pinned over scrollable consent copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with a concise, content-preserving consent surface and keep detailed settings available on demand.

findings.summary: The consent choice architecture makes rejection less clear and labels it as a paid option.
findings.evidence: The modal gives “Godkänn alla” a filled primary treatment while “Avvisa personanpassad reklam” is outlined and marked “Betaltjänst”; the copy also says rejection costs 49 kr/month on ad-funded services.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer accept and reject at equal prominence, remove misleading paid-choice labeling from the reject action, and separate subscription offers from privacy consent.

findings.summary: Many interactive text links have touch areas below the minimum target height.
findings.evidence: The target-size probe found 21 of 75 visible interactive elements below 24 px in at least one dimension, including “Läs mer” at 43×14 and multiple footer links at 18 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas with padding or pseudo-element target expansion while preserving visual density and spacing between adjacent controls.

findings.summary: Primary pages load slowly and the homepage is visually unstable.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 6.3 s and CLS 0.298; the article also had LCP 6.3 s. The raw-CDP trace corroborated a 5.07 s LCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP candidate, reserve late-content space, reduce critical dependency delay, and monitor field LCP/CLS by template.

findings.summary: Late content and animation cause substantial layout movement on the homepage.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.153 with repeated shifts between 3.3 and 4.1 seconds; Lighthouse measured 0.298 and reported 15 layout shifts.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for images, ads and delayed modules; use metric-compatible font fallbacks and avoid layout-affecting entrance motion.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is delayed by a large dependency graph and weak caching.
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 131 requests and 1.50 MB transferred. Lighthouse estimated 328 KiB homepage and 924 KiB article cache savings, plus up to 1,070 ms render-blocking savings on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical chains, cache immutable assets for longer, preconnect only essential origins, and prioritise the actual LCP resource.

findings.summary: The initial load ships substantial JavaScript that is unused during the tested journey.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 275 KiB unused JavaScript on the homepage and 182 KiB on the article; CMP, advertising, React and article bundles were leading sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load CMP details, advertising/media SDKs and below-fold interactive bundles only when their surfaces become relevant.

findings.summary: Some embedded and visual content lacks usable accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the iframe title audit on the homepage, and the image primitive reported 19 images without alt text (some decorative, but not all are clearly suppressed from accessibility APIs).
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful frames a title, provide contextual alt text for editorial images, and use empty alt only for confirmed decorative images.

findings.summary: Navigation and utility text fail WCAG contrast requirements.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured white-on-red mobile navigation at 3.9:1 and article breadcrumb red-on-dark at 4.27:1; the data-controller “Läs mer” link had only 2.41:1 contrast against surrounding text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the red/dark palette and utility-link styling to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and distinguish inline links beyond color.

findings.summary: The heading and skip-link structure is inconsistent across templates.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no h1. On the article, #skipNavigation links to #main but the metadata probe found no matching target, and Lighthouse failed the skip-link audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide one descriptive h1 per page and make the skip link target a stable, focusable main landmark on every template.

findings.summary: Anonymous page loads generate repeated failed session requests and console errors.
findings.evidence: HAR and both Lighthouse runs recorded three HTTP 400 responses from the Schibsted session/user-context endpoints, surfaced as browser console errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid requesting authenticated user context for anonymous sessions or handle expected anonymous responses without 400 network errors.

findings.summary: Several images do not reserve dimensions and some are oversized for display.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 7 images without width/height and 8 oversized images; Lighthouse independently failed its unsized-images audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height (or an equivalent aspect-ratio) and request responsive image widths matched to rendered size.

findings.summary: A generic privacy link does not describe its destination.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO found one link whose text is only “Läs mer”; otherwise viewport, crawlable hrefs and robots access passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use destination-specific link text such as “Läs personuppgiftspolicyn”.

findings.summary: A long-lived first-party cookie is set without Secure and both observed cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.evidence: The cookie primitive found abx2 without Secure and with SameSite=None for 365 days; _sp_su was Secure but also SameSite=None for 365 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every production cookie and use Lax or Strict unless cross-site delivery is demonstrably required; shorten retention where possible.

findings.summary: The pre-consent page establishes a broad third-party and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker primitive observed 20 third-party origins including ib.adnxs.com. HAR attributed 70 requests and 1.02 MB to third-party origins during the load.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential advertising and analytics until consent, consolidate vendors, batch measurement and remove origins that do not provide clear user value.

findings.summary: Image delivery still wastes resolution and misses basic loading optimisations.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 8 oversized images, 6 legacy-format images, 3 without srcset and 4 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the existing image CDN to emit AVIF/WebP, complete srcsets and sizes, lazy-load below-fold media, and match source dimensions to layout.

findings.summary: The initial page does disproportionate background and third-party work before the reader engages.
findings.evidence: The homepage loaded 75 scripts and contacted 20 third-party origins; scripts accounted for 778 KB transferred even while a consent wall prevented interaction with content.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer advertising, media players, account context and below-fold widgets until consent, visibility or user intent makes them necessary.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the transferred page budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party origins transferred 1,017,537 of 1,496,094 bytes (68%) and made 70 of 131 requests; CMP, media, React CDN and ad SDK resources were major contributors.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, lazy-load media and ads, and enforce the budget per page template in monitoring.

taskList.title: Make the consent experience non-blocking, balanced and separate from paid offers
Fix LCP, layout stability and critical resource delivery
Defer and budget third-party, advertising and unused JavaScript
Repair headings, skip navigation, names and contrast
Respect system theme and reduced-motion preferences
Optimise image sizing, formats and reserved dimensions
Opt eligible editorial navigation into View Transitions
